artifacts_produced.deploy_evidence: Moved the harvest-mode listing persist call (`_write_harvest_listings(client.listings)`) out of a post-loop position and into a `finally` wrapping the per-article `for article in client.articles(...)` loop, so it always runs with whatever `client.listings` holds the moment the loop stops -- normal exhaustion, the accepted-target break, or an exception raised from anywhere inside client.articles(). AMENDMENT 1 (row AMGT_HARVST-Z-S10): the persist call inside that `finally` is now itself wrapped in try/except -- `sys.exc_info()[0]` is read BEFORE the persist is attempted (reflecting the loop's own exit state), a failure is recorded as its own visible `harvest_listing_persist_failed` event, and the failure is re-raised only when nothing else was already propagating, so it can never displace an in-flight upstream exception. No other line in the loop body changed.

4 arms: a DRIVEN MID-LOOP RAISE (a fake harvest client captures 3 listing pages, raises UpstreamUnavailable(502) after 2 accepted articles) asserting all 3 pages landed in harvest_listing_outbox; a NEGATIVE CONTROL (load-bearing) reproducing the OLD post-loop-only placement with the SAME real _write_harvest_listings and the SAME real fake client on the SAME raise, proving the pages are LOST under that placement; and AC5's two arms -- the same mid-loop 502 driven with _write_harvest_listings itself made to raise sqlite3.OperationalError, asserting the ORIGINAL upstream exception still determines result["status"] with the persist failure surfaced as its own event; and the mirror arm (no propagating exception) asserting the SAME persist failure DOES surface as result["status"]=="error" when there is nothing to be subordinate to.
